answer: Divergent-Behavior Challenge. Each identity periodically submits a random seed; the network checks whether its responses to near-identical prompts drift like a karst landscape, unpredictably unique. A clone fleet sharing one policy produces near-identical outputs, so it fails. Each identity must sustain a pearl of behavioral entropy across a long island of trials. Cost: an attacker must run genuinely distinct policies, multiplying compute and maintenance per identity.
